items.title: Pahang coastline needs early action as erosion risks grow
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang's direct exposure to South China Sea makes its coastline increasingly vulnerable to stronger waves and extreme weather, highlighting the need for early action to tackle coastal erosion. The effects of coastal erosion are gradual but becoming increasingly visible, particularly along the southern part of Pahang. "Pekan, including Nenasi and Rompin, are among the areas showing signs of coastal erosion."

items.title: Pahang seeks RM850m to tackle erosion along 61km coastline
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Pahang government has implemented short- and long-term measures to address coastal erosion along 61km of coastline in the Pekan, Rompin and Kuantan districts. State Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim said the Irrigation and Drainage Department conducted studies and kept records to identify the causes of coastal erosion and determine appropriate measures. He said coastal erosion was a year-round issue requiring continuous monitoring and action, particularly where it could affect homes, public infrastructure and access routes.

items.title: Waves sweep away home, memories in Rompin village [WATCH]
items.summary: The three-room house was sponsored by a financial institution for her family in 2009. They did not expect giant waves during the monsoon season on Jan 12 last year to bring down one of its walls, forcing them to leave the village. During the incident last year, the sea was barely 20m away.

items.title: MLS fines Messi for striking an opponent
items.summary: MIAMI: Major League Soccer fined Inter Miami's Argentine superstar Lionel Messi an undisclosed amount on Friday for slapping Philadelphia's Quinn Sullivan on the back of the neck in the clubs' 2-2 draw on Wednesday. Miami's Ian Fray was fined an undisclosed amount for the same infraction. Dujic did send off Cavan Sullivan, younger brother and teammate of Quinn, and Miami's Italian midfielder Yannick Bright after their stoppage time scuffle in Miami's penalty area.

items.title: RM700,000 seaside dream swept away by coastal erosion [WATCH]
items.summary: Tourism entrepreneur Edde Firdaus Abdul Aziz had invested some RM700,000 to acquire 1ha of coastal land, transforming it into Kekunang Tering Chalet, a nature getaway featuring seven chalets, including a tree house and tube cabins fashioned from concrete culverts. But the dream lasted only about six years before relentless coastal erosion claimed the structures one by one. Edde Firdaus, 46, said the sea had since devoured much of the land, leaving just 0.4ha, with the remaining ground continuing to disappear.

items.title: Trump announces temporary tariff relief on ground beef imports
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump announced on Friday that the United States would temporarily allow a greater volume of foreign beef imports, in his latest bid to lower costs for American consumers as midterm elections approach. The US cattle herd has shrunk to its lowest level since the 1950s – in part due to drought and international competition – with the diminishing numbers pushing beef product prices higher. 'DISAPPOINTED' US cattle and rancher groups have been resistant to importing more beef.

items.title: Pahang coastline under siege as erosion threatens homes, roads and livelihoods [WATCH]
items.summary: KUANTAN: Along Pahang's 210km coastline spanning three districts — Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin — the South China Sea is steadily reshaping the boundary between land and water, alarming coastal communities. Strong waves have severely damaged and eroded the shorelines of at least 10 locations in Pahang, including popular beaches Pantai Cherating and Teluk Chempedak, as well as beaches in Pekan and Rompin. Other affected areas include Pantai Balok, Pantai Kempadang, Pantai Sepat and Pantai Cherok Paloh in Kuantan; Tanjung Batu in Pekan; and Kuala Rompin, Tanjung Gemok and Kampung Mukut on Pulau Tioman in Rompin.

items.title: Rocky case, Maju Junction deaths and Singaporean kidnapping among key court cases this week
items.summary: KLANG: A tussle between a volunteer dog-catcher and a housewife over a dog named Rocky on July 29 ended with both being charged with animal cruelty at the Klang Sessions Court on Thursday. On Thursday, parcel delivery rider Muhammad Shah Idham Nor Haikal Shaharom,24, was charged with unreasonably choking Rocky using a loop rope while and S. Roghini Devi, 42, was charged with unreasonably pulling it, causing pain to the animal. Meanwhile, at the magistrate's court, Roghini pleaded guilty to failing to obtain a dog license for Rocky, an offence under Section 3 of the Klang Royal City Council's Dog Licensing and Dog Breeding House By-Laws.

items.title: Genting heist, child trafficking, woman burnt among major crimes this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still hunting three masked men who made off with jewellery worth about RM1.7 million in a daring two-minute heist at a goldsmith in SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, on Monday. Police activated Ops Tutup, setting up roadblocks at entry and exit points at the hilltop resort and along the route towards Batang Kali. Police rescued 17 Jordanian children aged between three months and 14 years believed to have been forced to beg at busy tourist and commercial areas in the city.

items.title: Explainer: What we know about the door handles that triggered China's record auto recall
items.summary: DETROIT: Electronic door handles of the kind at the centre of China's largest-ever vehicle recall have proliferated across the globe over the past decade, especially on electric vehicles. Tesla and eight other automakers said on Friday they will recall a total of about 4.3 million vehicles in China over concerns that their doors may be difficult to open in an emergency. Popularised by Tesla, the door handles are designed to sit flush with the body of the door, for a minimalist look that also reduces aerodynamic drag.

items.title: From a Penang home kitchen to nationwide favourite: The story of Jeruk Madu Pak Ali
items.summary: More than four decades later, Jeruk Madu Pak Ali has grown from a three-person operation to a business with four production plants in Simpang Ampat on mainland Penang with over 100 employees and 50 retail outlets nationwide. Together, the facilities produce about 300 tonnes of pickled fruits every month. Jeruk Madu Pak Ali’s marketing and public relations executive Mohd Shahrul Nizam Shahidin showing the packaged pickled fruits and the traditional trades certificate from Penang Global Tourism.

items.title: US, Canada push to seal trade deal as deadline nears
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US and Canadian negotiators raced against the clock on Friday to reach a trade deal before a midnight deadline when punishing new US tariffs are set to kick in. In the latest salvo amid months of trade hostility, US President Donald Trump threatened to impose new 50 per cent duties on a range of Canadian products by Wednesday. Hours before the new deadline, Trump said the US "should be able to have a deal with Canada", citing his "good relationship" with Prime Minister Mark Carney.

items.title: One dead after Canada plane hits car
items.summary: MONTREAL: One person has been killed in western Canada after a small passenger plane struck a vehicle while making an emergency landing on a road, police said. The incident occurred on Thursday afternoon in Prince George, British Columbia, more than 700 kilometres (435 miles) north of Vancouver. "Police are saddened to confirm that there has been one fatality in this incident, an occupant of one of the vehicles," the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said in a statement.

items.title: TikTok to pay US$400m settlement in US children's privacy case
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: TikTok and parent company ByteDance have agreed to pay US$400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform violated federal children's privacy laws, the department announced on Friday. "Under the settlement, TikTok will pay US$300 million immediately and an additional US$100 million upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered against TikTok's predecessor, Musical.ly," the department said in a statement. COPPA bars websites from gathering the personal information of children younger than 13 without parental permission.

items.title: Pentagon fires Stars and Stripes leaders after they criticise interference
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Pentagon on Friday fired the editor-in-chief and publisher of the Stars and Stripes newspaper, which has covered the US military since the Civil War, according to the publication's leadership, which spoke to US media. The department stated earlier this year that it was seeking to steer Stars and Stripes coverage away from "woke distractions". Max Lederer, who has served as the publication's publisher since 2007 and had announced his retirement just three days earlier, was also notified that he was being terminated, according to CBS.

items.title: Netherlands fines Uber US$960 million over driver account suspensions
items.summary: AMSTERDAM: The Netherlands has fined ride-hailing giant Uber 825 million euros (US$960 million) for having deactivated drivers' accounts without informing them. The ruling is based on European data regulations which state that people should not "be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing." It began with a complaint against Uber filed in France, but the case was heard in the Netherlands because the US car-booking giant's European headquarters are in Amsterdam.

items.title: Brazil's Lula urges tariffs resolution in call with Trump
items.summary: BRASÍLIA: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio da Silva urged US President Donald Trump in a phone call Friday to resolve their countries' trade dispute, saying US tariffs were imposed on "baseless" grounds. Washington imposed two new rounds of tariffs on the Latin American giant in July over alleged unfair trade practices, a move that has become a key campaign issue ahead of an October presidential election in Brazil. Trump has backed several victorious right-wing candidates in Latin America recently and is an ally of Brazil's jailed far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, whose son Flavio is Lula's main rival in the election.

items.title: Sword-wielding attacker wounds at least two teens at Swedish school
items.summary: STOCKHOLM: At least two teenagers were seriously wounded after a sword-wielding attacker entered a high school in central Sweden, authorities said, while media reported the perpetrator had been shot by police. Regional healthcare director Jonas Cederberg told AFP two "seriously wounded" people had been admitted to hospital. Police said they had received reports of the attack just after 2pm (1200 GMT).

items.title: UK, Canada, Australia slam Israel ending probe into aid worker killings
items.summary: LONDON: Britain, Canada, and Australia on Friday condemned as "shameful" Israel's decision to close an investigation into the death of seven aid workers killed in Gaza in 2024. Israel's military called the incident a "tragic mistake." "Israel extends its condolences to the families of the seven World Central Kitchen aid workers... who tragically lost their lives under deeply regrettable circumstances," Israel's foreign ministry posted on X on Friday.

items.title: US-sanctioned ICC head warns against 'demise of international rule of law'
items.summary: TOKYO: International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane of Japan warned on Friday against "the demise of international rule of law" after the United States targeted her with sanctions. Akane's statement – her first public comments since the sanctions – comes after the ICC on Wednesday called the US measures a "flagrant attack" on the court's independence. Washington's latest move follows sanctions it imposed on several ICC officials, seen as largely in response to the court's investigations involving Israel, a US ally.

items.title: Indonesia arrests 10 Myanmar nationals following liquid meth bust
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia has arrested 10 Myanmar nationals in a drug bust involving 2.6 metric tonnes of liquid methamphetamine found on a ship sailing with a Tanzanian flag, authorities said at a press conference on Friday. The drugs were found in a water tank and eight 200-litre drums hidden on top of a container on the ship, Indonesia's National Narcotics Agency chief Suyudi Ario Seto said. Indonesia has strict drug laws, with some offences punishable by death.

items.title: Swiss man jailed for insulting Hindu holiday in Indonesia
items.summary: DENPASAR: Swiss authorities said Friday they were providing consular support to a national sentenced to one year in prison in Indonesia for insulting a Hindu religious day while he was on holiday in Bali. Luzian Andrin Zgraggen, 26, was sentenced on Thursday after being found guilty of crimes under an Indonesian law against online hate speech, I Wayan Suarta, a spokesman for the court in Denpasar, told AFP. On that day each year, the Hindu-majority island largely comes to a standstill, with work, travel, public entertainment and even electricity use discouraged for locals and tourists alike.

items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan want Hormuz Strait kept open, safe amid Iran-US tensions
items.summary: The position was conveyed during a phone call between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Pakistani counterpart Shehbaz Sharif today. On bilateral ties, Anwar and Shehbaz agreed to intensify trade and economic cooperation, which still had significant potential, including expanding Pakistani meat exports to Malaysia. Earlier, Shehbaz asked Anwar about his health.

items.title: Russian social network sues Apple over App Store removals
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russian social network VK said on Friday that it had filed a lawsuit against Apple with the Moscow Arbitration Court, demanding that the company's apps be reinstated in the App Store, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. According to court documents, VK LLC filed the claim with the Moscow Arbitration Court against United States (US)-based Apple Inc., Russian Apple Rus LLC and Ireland-based Apple Distribution International Ltd., although the subject and grounds of the claims have not yet been disclosed in the documents. Apple unilaterally removed VK's apps from the App Store without warning, VK claimed.

items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan sign treaty allowing prisoners to serve sentences at home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Pakistan today signed the International Transfer of Prisoners (ITOP) Treaty, strengthening legal and security cooperation between the two countries. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the treaty was signed with Pakistan's Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi following his courtesy call on Pakistan Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif. The signing ceremony was held at the Prime Minister's Office in Pakistan and witnessed by Shehbaz.

items.title: NST Leader: Plugging the gaps in border security
items.summary: FOR decades, drug cartels have developed sophisticated methods to evade detection, favouring deep-sea transit and commercial container fraud because the bigger payloads mean bountiful profits. One enduring method relies on drug mules. These drug mules fall into three categories.

items.title: Netanyahu calls Turkiye's Erdogan 'antisemitic dictator'
items.summary: JERUSALEM: The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday called Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an "antisemitic dictator" and vowed Israel would "continue to act forcefully against Turkiye's attempts to destabilise the region." Netanyahu had said Turkiye was looking to establish a military presence there, but Turkiye has denied any visit to the site. "Israel has long been unimpressed by Turkiye's hypocrisy.

items.title: Harry's UK return raises more questions than answers
items.summary: DOZENS of questions swirled on Thursday as Prince Harry prepares to move back to the United Kingdom with his wife and children, six years after his departure sparked a bitter rift with the royal family. "Meghan's cookery series didn't go well. And also, they lost Spotify," royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams said.

items.title: The haze is man-made, the suffering is shared
items.summary: Two heavy afternoon downpours earlier this week in Kuching did little more than give the city short respites from the chocking haze enveloping it and much of Sarawak. A politician in Serian — the nearest main town to the Kalimantan border — even suggested that reparations be requested from Indonesia, where the haze, as a result of uncontrolled forest fires, mostly originates. The haze has been rather subdued in recent years.

items.title: Health Ministry sets 3 priorities for 2027 Budget
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Health Ministry (MOH) has identified three main clusters for Budget 2027 — strengthening healthcare services for the people, enhancing national resilience, and promoting social justice and development for all. The ministry said the priorities were discussed during its Budget 2027 Engagement Session here today. "MOH also stressed that every allocation must be outcome- and impact-oriented, rather than merely focusing on the amount of expenditure.

items.title: Penang Health Dept apologises over long waits at hospital ER
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Health Department has apologised for long waiting times at Penang Hospital's Emergency and Trauma Department following a viral video posted on social media. The department said it took note of the video, which circulated on the night of Aug 20, highlighting lengthy waiting times at the hospital's emergency department. He said patients were categorised into three zones — Red for critical cases requiring immediate treatment, Yellow for semi-critical cases requiring urgent medical attention and Green for non-emergency cases involving mild or non-critical symptoms.

items.title: Tebrau MP to raise in Parliament tax uncertainty over commingled oil cargo
items.summary: He said the matter required clarification from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD) to ensure industry players had clarity and certainty regarding their tax obligations. As such, I hope and urge the Royal Customs to provide greater clarity on this matter to industry players. Puah said he would raise the matter in Parliament to seek clarification on the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo operations.

items.title: Independent review, not blind denial, needed to address US transshipment claims, says maritime trade expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Malaysia should conduct an independent review into allegations by the United States (US) concerning transshipment activities to ensure any violations are identified while protecting the country’s reputation, according to Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan. The maritime expert said the review must trace the complete movement of the cargo, including the manifest, bill of lading, Customs documentation, certificate of origin, storage records, any blending or processing carried out and the final declaration before export. “Malaysia must respond quickly with evidence, independent verification and a clear enforcement position.

items.title: Zahid: Melaka election strategy cannot mirror Johor, Negeri Sembilan, needs tailored formula
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Barisan Nasional (BN) needs a formula suitable to Melaka’s geopolitical landscape in the upcoming state election, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said any negotiations must take into account two aspects, namely benefits and drawbacks. He said political cooperation at the state level should also be seen in the context of efforts to strengthen political stability at the national level.

items.title: Anwar lands in Brunei for 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation, to meet Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here today for a two-day working visit to attend the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC-27) between Malaysia and Brunei. The special aircraft carrying Anwar and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, landed at Brunei International Airport at 6.10pm. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Brunei was recorded at RM5.86 billion (US$1.37 billion), with exports to Brunei valued at RM4.20 billion (US$0.98 billion) and imports at RM1.66 billion (US$0.39 billion).

items.title: Sarawak haze fight hinges on suitable clouds, Uggah says seeding useless without them
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 21 — Cloud seeding operations to tackle the haze will depend on favourable weather conditions, particularly the presence of suitable clouds, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas. The State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman said discussions had been held with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), which was ready to conduct the cloud seeding operation whenever weather conditions permit. Uggah expressed hope that weather conditions would improve soon, allowing the cloud seeding operation to be carried out and help tackle the haze.

items.title: Perhilitan captures giant 5.5‑metre crocodile after May attack injured retired policeman in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 21 — The Negeri Sembilan Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) captured a 500kg crocodile measuring 5.5 metres in Sungai Tanjung Agas, Sungai Linggi, today. Its director, Wan Mat Wan Harun, said the female crocodile, estimated at 70 years old, was captured in a trap placed in the area two days ago. “Perhilitan set a crocodile trap at the site on Wednesday following a report about the reptile in Tanjung Agas.

items.title: Court of Appeal spares two men gallows, orders 30 years jail plus 12 rotan strokes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — Two men escaped the gallows after the Court of Appeal substituted their death sentences with 30 years’ imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane each for drug trafficking. The decision was made by a three-member panel comprising Datuk Azmi Ariffin (now a Federal Court judge), Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, who dismissed Muhamad Nor Aziz and Muhamad Shafiq Aliff Mazlan’s appeals against their convictions. Judge Meor Hashimi said the two appellants had instead received a fair and impartial trial and were given adequate opportunity to defend themselves by the trial judge.

items.title: Zahid urges Malaysian bikers abroad to obey host laws after Hat Yai summons row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Malaysian motorsport enthusiasts travelling abroad must abide by the laws and regulations of their host countries, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said mutual respect, tolerance and an understanding of neighbouring countries’ regulations were crucial to maintaining good relations among Asean member states. Ahmad Zahid said this when met by reporters after the closing ceremony of the Negeri Sembilan Contingent Charity Ride programme with the Ipoh Super Bike Club (ISBC) in conjunction with the 219th Police Day and 69th Merdeka Eve celebrations at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters here today.

items.title: Chow says Penang awaits DAP leadership call before equal constituency law move
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Aug 21 — Penang will await a decision from DAP’s national leadership before considering any move to introduce an Equal Constituency Development Enactment in the state, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said opposition representatives regularly raise the matter during State Legislative Assembly sittings and seek higher allocations. Chow said opposition assemblymen currently receive RM60,000 in allocation.

items.title: Police vow transparent Tabung Haji investigations, warn public against speculation or rumours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), through its Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID), has opened five investigation papers into cases involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), including matters raised in the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report. CCID director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said 127 people had so far had their statements recorded to assist the investigations. He said the investigations were being conducted under several laws, including the Penal Code, Tabung Haji Act 1995, Companies Act 1965 and Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).

items.title: Foreign minister says Asean best platform as Malaysia pushes regional action on haze crisis
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 21 — Malaysia will utilise Asean diplomatic channels to seek a solution to the transboundary haze affecting several areas in the region, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said Asean remains the most appropriate platform for addressing issues involving countries in the region. “NRES Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup will also write to his counterpart in Indonesia.

items.title: Rapid KL to run 24‑hour trains and buses for Merdeka Eve and National Day crowds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Selected rail and bus services operated by Rapid KL will operate 24 hours on Aug 30 and 31 to facilitate public movement in conjunction with the 2026 National Day celebrations. Rapid KL in a statement today announced that the extension of operating hours involves all its rail services, namely the Light Rail Transit (LRT), Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Kuala Lumpur Monorail. “The Sunway BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) Line, along with several bus routes and Rapid KL On-Demand (ROD), will also operate 24 hours, providing more travel options to the public throughout the celebration period.

items.title: Ten GOF personnel detained in Penang extortion probe involving e-waste factory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Ten General Operations Force (GOF) personnel from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) were detained yesterday to assist investigations into an extortion case at an electronic waste processing factory in Tasik Gelugor, Penang. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (Operations) deputy director Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said all the personnel involved were stationed at the GOF 2nd Battalion in Kulim, Kedah. Any officer or personnel involved in any crime, the force’s management will take appropriate action without favouritism,” he told a press conference here today.

items.title: Company MD says he handed Hamzah Zainudin’s former aide RM350,000 cash in paper bags after firm won police tender
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — A witness told the Sessions Court today that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad asked him to pay RM350,000 in cash as part of a five per cent commission after helping Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NXG) secure a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender. “Sayed (Sayed Amir Muzzakkir) contacted me and asked me, ‘Can you pay 350k?, I need to use this money, cash.’ “I also informed Sayed that I would pay in two instalments and Sayed agreed to that proposal,” said the main prosecution witness while reading his witness statement at the corruption trial of Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, who is facing three charges involving RM350,000.

items.title: PAS tells BN to choose between Perikatan and Pakatan in Melaka
items.summary: MARANG, Aug 21 — PAS President Abdul Hadi Awang said Perikatan Nasional is fully prepared to walk away from Barisan Nasional (BN) should its partner flirt with an alliance with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka state election. Hadi said that while the PN coalition remains confident in its ability to deploy a range of tactical alternatives, high-level discussions regarding cooperation with BN for the Melaka polls remain ongoing, NST reported. Hadi further observed that the complexities faced during the Johor state election appear to have subsided, making the path toward a Melaka alliance more straightforward.

items.title: Afternoon checks show nine Sarawak areas with unhealthy air quality, Serian still very unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Air Pollution Index (API) reading at Serian station in Sarawak reached 227 (very unhealthy) as of 2pm today, while nine other areas in the state recorded unhealthy readings. She said air quality nationwide had deteriorated today, with an increase in areas recording unhealthy API readings in Sarawak due to haze moving in from various directions. “The National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan have been activated to coordinate action among government agencies in addressing open burning and dealing with the national haze situation,” she said.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Witness says MOF wanted open tender, PMO insisted on direct negotiation, pre‑qualification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) had initially wanted government projects under the Bumiputera contractors' programme Jana Wibawa to be carried out through open tender, but the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) had instructed for Jana Wibawa projects to be given out either by direct negotiation or through a pre-qualification tender, a senior MOF officer said today. At the time of the Jana Wibawa programme during Muhyiddin's administration, Rosni was the deputy under secretary of the same division and also chaired a Finance Ministry committee that evaluated whether proposed contractors forwarded by the PMO were qualified to be given Jana Wibawa projects. "Initially, Jana Wibawa, we wanted to carry out through open tender, but we received instructions from PMO.

items.title: MOH bans three batches of Chomel hand sanitiser over excessive methanol content
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has banned the sale of Chomel Hand Sanitizer after three batches of the product were found to contain methanol above the permitted limit. As such, the MOH urged the public not to purchase or use products from the affected batches. “Uncontrolled exposure to methanol can pose serious health risks.

items.title: Police arrest drug suspect after struggle with machete leaves officer injured in Jeli
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 21 — A suspect believed to be involved in drug trafficking was arrested after brandishing a machete at police officers and injuring one during a raid in Kampung Lubok Bongor, Jeli, yesterday. Jeli police chief Supt Kamarulzaman Harun said the 11am incident took place when a team from the district police Criminal Investigation Division raided an unnumbered house in the village. “The suspect acted aggressively by pulling out a machete tucked at his waist and brandishing it at the police officers while threatening to kill.

items.title: Six charged with kidnapping Singaporean man for S$20,000 ransom in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 21 — Six individuals including a woman pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of kidnapping a Singaporean man, 32, for the purpose of obtaining a ransom of S$20,000 (RM63,000), earlier this month. M. Balamurugan, 46, K. Saravanan, 40, P. Sri Devi, 41, G. Puganeswaran, 38, S. Gobinath, 38, and X. Adwin Nicholas, 41, made the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Nor Aziati Jaafar. The charges were brought under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961 and read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for a prison sentence of up to 40 years and whipping, if convicted.

items.title: High Court proceeds with Duta Enclave assessment as Semantan Estate weighs secret settlement terms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Putrajaya’s offer to compensate Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd without a formal assessment exercise remains open, though the company has yet to provide a response, according to a senior federal counsel. Last week, Semantan applied to postpone the hearing to evaluate the government’s proposal, but Justice Roslan Mat Nor rejected the application, allowing the assessment of compensation to proceed. The appeals court also mandated an assessment of mesne profits — compensation for the loss of use of the property.

items.title: Anwar asks Indonesia’s Prabowo to intercede in Felda's RM2.5b PT Eagle High loss
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reached out formally to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, requesting special intervention regarding Felda’s investments in Indonesia, specifically involving PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk (EHP). This is one example,” Anwar said. The PM disclosed these details during a Friendly Session with Felda’s top management and managers today.

items.title: Anwar: Action against Tabung Haji, Felda based on wrongdoing, not religion or race
items.summary: KAJANG, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected claims that the government’s scrutiny of Tabung Haji (TH) is driven by the institution’s Islamic identity, insisting that any action taken is a response to mismanagement and wrongdoing, not religious or racial targeting. Speaking at a programme with Felda’s top management today, Anwar said the same principle applied across the board, citing Felda as another example of an institution closely associated with the Malay community that has faced government intervention over past failures, FMT reported. “Some Islamic party leaders say action is mainly being taken against Malay-Muslim agencies.

items.title: Government agency chairman among five remanded in MACC probe over alleged below-market land sale
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 21 — The Magistrate’s Court here today granted a four-day remand order for five individuals, including the chairman of a government agency with the title of Datuk, to assist in an investigation into suspected abuse of position involving the disposal of land. Magistrate Noor Idayu Salim issued the remand order following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted yesterday, saying the case was being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Penang Hill cable car hits 32pc completion; operations expected by late 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 21 — The Penang Hill cable car project has reached 32 per cent completion and is expected to be physically finished by August next year, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. Speaking during a monitoring visit from the Botanic Gardens to the summit of Penang Hill, Chow noted that the project has entered a more promising phase following the completion of all underground works. “We expect the work to progress faster because above-ground construction is easier to control compared with underground works,” Chow said.

items.title: Felda task force to examine current management, not just past problems, says Anwar
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would wait for the complete report of the Special Task Force investigating the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA) before making any official announcement. He said the special task force had begun its work and the findings of the investigation were expected to be presented in the near future. “(Its aspects include) all matters regarding management, improving management... of course identifying past problems, but what is important is current management and way forward,” he said.

items.title: Singaporean man jailed for insulting Islam during e-hailing trip in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 21 — A 56-year-old Singaporean man has been jailed for 14 days and fined RM7,000 after admitting to demeaning Islam during a trip in Johor Bahru last month. Mohamed Anim Atam pleaded guilty to the charges before Magistrate A. Shaarmini. The incident occurred at approximately 5pm on July 30, as the accused travelled from Jalan Tun Razak to Jalan Meldrum.

items.title: Airbnb crackdown: Penang introduces new licensing laws for short-term rentals
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 20 — Penang has introduced a new regulatory framework to govern short-term rentals of private accommodations, including Airbnbs and homestays, effective August 1. State local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye announced that the Penang Private Short-term Accommodation By-Laws 2026 now require all TIP operators to obtain official licences from their respective city councils. Previously, local authorities lacked the legal teeth to take action against unlicensed operators.

items.title: Malaysia targets first ‘made by Malaysia’ chips using Arm Limited technology by 2030, says economy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The government is targeting 2030 for the first “Made by Malaysia” chips developed using Arm Limited technology to enter production and the semiconductor supply chain. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said four companies have so far begun designing chips using technology from British semiconductor technology company Arm Limited, with the aim of eventually bringing their products into production and the semiconductor supply chain. Akmal said eight Arm technology-access packages — comprising four Arm CSS and four Arm Flexible Access tokens — had so far been offered to five local companies.
